Internship in Urban Design Workshop

Technical University of Ostrava, Czech Republic

  • Starts on Feb 1st - 10th
  • Duration 2 Weeks
  • Tuition Free

About the Host University

VSB – Technical University of Ostrava, Czech Republic

Established in 1849, VSB–Technical University of Ostrava (VSB–TUO) is one of the oldest and most reputed public technical universities in the Czech Republic, known for excellence in engineering, technology, and applied research. The university is home to IT4Innovations National Supercomputing Center, housing the powerful Karolina supercomputer. With advanced research facilities, strong industry collaborations, and practical learning opportunities, VSB–TUO offers a world-class technical education. The Architecture Department at VSB–TUO combines creative architectural design with modern engineering and sustainable construction technologies. Key areas include sustainable architecture, energy-efficient buildings, Building Information Modelling (BIM), innovative construction materials, and urban planning. Students gain valuable practical exposure through design workshops, industry-oriented projects, and modern construction techniques, preparing them for careers in architecture and the built environment.

Location

About Czech Republic

The Czech Republic (Czechia) is a developed Central European country and a member of the European Union and Schengen Area, renowned for its architectural heritage, advanced engineering, and high-quality education. Its capital, Prague, is famous for Gothic, Baroque, and Renaissance architecture, including the iconic Charles Bridge and Prague Castle. Home to Charles University (1348), one of Europe’s oldest universities, Czechia offers excellent opportunities in architecture, civil engineering, sustainable construction, and urban planning. Czechia is internationally recognised for Czech Cubism, represented by Prague’s House of the Black Madonna (1912), and Functionalist Architecture, exemplified by the UNESCO-listed Villa Tugendhat (1930). Its engineering heritage includes the historic Negrelli Viaduct (1850), a remarkable railway bridge. Czech scientist Otto Wichterle invented modern soft contact lenses, while Jaroslav Heyrovský won the 1959 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for polarography. The word “Robot” also originated from Czech literature, reflecting the country’s rich history of scientific and technological innovation.

Day-wise Program

What each day looks like

  • Format 8 working days (Mon–Fri + Mon–Wed), weekend free
  • Dates Feb 1 - Feb 10 2027
  • Participants Max. 24 students,
    8 teams of 3
  • Language English
  • Venue Department of Architecture studios; field work in Ostrava
  1. 01

    Introduction

    Day 1 · Mon
    • Morning Welcome and organisation of the programme. Introduction to VSB–TUO, the Faculty of Civil Engineering and the Department of Architecture. Lecture: Ostrava – historical development, present-day form and urban structure of the city. Lecture · 2 h
    • Afternoon Guided tour of Ostrava: Lower Vítkovice (industrial heritage), historic city centre, selected notable buildings. Field

    OutputOrientation in the city

  2. 02

    Workshop brief

    Day 2 · Tue
    • Morning Presentation of the workshop task: the site, expected outputs, examples of results, handover of background materials (maps, plans, data). Formation of teams. Lecture · 2 h
    • Afternoon Self-guided site visit by teams: first observations, photo documentation, sketches. Field

    OutputTeams, background materials · Site record

  3. 03

    Site analysis

    Day 3 · Wed
    • Morning The site in context: history, planning framework, key data. Method: how to draw a problem map (values, problems, potentials, conflicts) and what it should lead to. Lecture · 2 h
    • Afternoon Team work on site analysis and problem map; consultations. ◆ Studio

    OutputProblem map (draft)

  4. 04

    Starting points

    Day 4 · Thu
    • Morning Team presentations: what we know about the site, key problems and potentials, starting points and assumptions for the design. Discussion and feedback. Review
    • Afternoon Possible approaches to the site: first concepts and variants of the urban structure. ◆ Studio

    OutputProblem map, design assumptions · Concept sketches

  5. 05

    Urban economics and regulation

    Day 5 · Fri
    • Morning Urban economics: how much to build, density and intensity of use, balance indicators (population, gross floor area, share of public space, mix of uses), basic social and economic indicators and costs. Spatial regulation: principles of regulation and the regulation plan (building lines, heights, plot coverage, public space). Lecture · 2 h
    • Afternoon Testing the variants against the balance indicators; choice of the concept and its basic rules. ◆ Studio

    OutputSelected concept + first figures

  6. 06

    Balance

    Day 6 · Mon
    • Morning How to compile the balance table: areas, gross floor area, population, public space, rough financial estimate. Linking the figures to the urban design. Lecture · 2 h
    • Afternoon Development of the urban design, regulation drawing and balance table; consultations. ◆ Studio

    OutputUrban design + balance table (draft)

  7. 07

    Presentation

    Day 7 · Tue
    • Morning How to produce the final output: formal drawings, graphic presentation and layout of panels. Lecture · 2 h
    • Afternoon Finalising drawings, balance table and presentation panels; consultations. ◆ Studio

    OutputFinal panels

  8. 08

    Final presentation

    Day 8 · Wed
    • Morning Final presentations of team proposals and discussion with the review panel. Review
    • Afternoon Feedback on the programme, certificates of completion, closing. Panels displayed as a short exhibition. Closing

    OutputFinal presentation · Certificate

◆ One studio afternoon between Days 3 and 7 is replaced by a visit to a building under construction or a completed building in Ostrava, scheduled according to availability. Site and exact dates to be confirmed.
